name: Ween
label: Twin/Tone
lede: Two guys and a DAT machine from New Hope, Pennsylvania, spent forty years making the sound of a band that will play anything, and you can't tell when they're joking.

eras.title: Typing class, four-tracks, a tape called Boognish
eras.text: Two kids who don't like each other end up at adjacent keyboards in New Hope, Pennsylvania, and spend five years making cassettes nobody asked for. By the end of the decade they're opening for the Butthole Surfers at Trenton's City Gardens and a Twin/Tone scout has noticed.

years.cap: Ween at Ryman Auditorium, Nashville 10.16.2018 · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Two kids who don't like each other meet in typing class
years.p: Aaron Freeman and Mickey Melchiondo land in the same junior high class in New Hope, Pennsylvania, and become Gene Ween and Dean Ween.
years.xp:
Freeman remembered it plainly: "We didn't like each other. He was a jock, and I was more of a trench-coat guy." Per Wikipedia, the band name mashes together the words "wuss" and "penis".

Four years of self-released cassettes followed, including Mrs. Slack (1984), Erica Peterson's Flaming Crib Death (1986), The Crucial Squeegie Lip (1987) and Axis: Bold as Boognish (1988). Their public debut, in 1986, was a Jimi Hendrix cover at the New Hope-Solebury High School talent show, with Chris Williams on bass and Karl Weimer on drums.

years.cap: Ween (1993).jpg, the Charlotte, Leicester 1993 More from the Charlotte... · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers
years.h: John and Peter's, City Gardens, and a bill with the Butthole Surfers
years.p: By 1988 Gene and Dean are regulars at John and Peter's in New Hope and at City Gardens in Trenton, New Jersey.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists [[Butthole Surfers|2339bc21-aa92-4850-86f0-4bb9433910c8]] and [[They Might Be Giants|183d6ef6-e161-47ff-9085-063c8b897e97]] among the acts they opened for. Dean, meanwhile, was publishing a fanzine called Yuck and working the Trenton punk scene, Magnet reports.

The live act was two guys, two guitars and a DAT machine playing the backing tracks. That was the entire band until 1994.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers
years.h: Twin/Tone signs a band with no drummer
years.p: A&R man Dave Ayers gets Ween onto Minneapolis indie Twin/Tone. Wikipedia says he caught them opening for Skunk in Maplewood, New Jersey.
years.xp: Magnet tells it differently: Twin/Tone signed them after a summer 1988 party show in New Jersey. Either way, Ayers ended up managing them as well.

eras.title: Twin/Tone, Kramer, and a bong-headed Leonard Cohen
eras.text: The first record is on Twin/Tone, the second is on somebody else's label, and by the end of 1992 Elektra has them. Along the way a Fugazi crowd boos them and Beavis and Butt-Head don't.

years.src: The Varsity: A conversation with Dean Ween from 1996 · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Opening for Fugazi, and roughly 1,200 people boo
years.p: Dean says it was the worst reception Ween ever got.
years.xp:
Dean told The Varsity in 1996 that around 1,200 people booed the set at a [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] show, the harshest reaction they had ever gotten. The source doesn't pin the date beyond about 1989 to 1990.

That same February 1990, per Wikipedia, [[Henry Rollins|656b39fb-979c-4c57-bb87-61d1a8eb38d1]] faced a cool City Gardens crowd after Ween's set and told them to "start liking them now".

years.src: Wikipedia: GodWeenSatan: The Oneness · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: GodWeenSatan: The Oneness: 26 tracks on Twin/Tone
years.p: The debut packs in songs from their first six years; "You Fucked Up" and "Fat Lenny" become live staples.
years.xp:
Dean later called the album a greatest-hits collection. [[Andrew Weiss|afdb875c-cca9-4556-87c1-62f635688b13]] produced, and it was cut in 1989 and 1990 at places including the Zion House of Flesh in Hopewell, New Jersey. Ween's first overseas shows followed in the Netherlands, December 1990 into January 1991.

Pitchfork later gave it a 9.6; Robert Christgau was less impressed.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pod · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: The Pod appears on [[Kramer|d898e082-70d1-4a86-ac8e-ecdf89892994]]'s label, not Twin/Tone's
years.p: Recorded on a Tascam four-track in the duo's apartment on Van Sant Road, Solebury Township, and released on Shimmy-Disc.
years.xp:
The sessions ran January to October 1990. The cover is a parody of Leonard Cohen's The Best of Leonard Cohen with Chris Williams's head, bong and all, over Cohen's. Wikipedia says both members had mononucleosis while recording, and the band dismissed drug theories as "the most slime-bag thing we could think of".

Magnet reports Kramer paid them $2,500 and took them to Jamaica, and quotes Dean on the label situation: "We breached our contract, which only a 19- or 20-year-old would have the balls to do." Weiss produced and mixed. After the first US and UK tours they recorded for John Peel at the BBC in February 1992. Aphex Twin later listed The Pod among his ten favorite albums, Wikipedia says; Elektra reissued it in 1995.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pure Guava · Wikipedia: Dean Ween
years.h: Pure Guava: the Elektra debut, still made like a home tape
years.p: It sells 65,000 copies in its first six months, per Wikipedia, and the Ween of the four-track era is now on a major.
years.xp: Guy Heller of [[Moistboyz|3867cba4-766a-4646-befd-010d053551ad]] sings lead on "Flies on My Dick"; Dean and Heller had started Moistboyz in 1991. "Big Jilm" was inspired by a car dealership employee named James A. Lemons, and "Poop Ship Destroyer" grew into a live jam vehicle.

eras.title: Beavis and Butt-Head, a drummer, a soul record
eras.text: MTV's dumbest cartoon delivers an actual hit, the DAT machine retires, and a fierce live band shows up. Then comes a soul album, and a country album Elektra didn't see coming.

years.cap: Ween spiller i en konsert · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Pure Guava · Wikipedia: Ween
yt: Beavis and Butt-Head watch Push th' Little Daisies
years.h: Beavis and Butt-Head watch "Push th' Little Daisies"
years.p: The clip gets heavy MTV play, and after a 1993 tour of Australia the single climbs to number 18 there.
years.xp: The radio edit swaps the profanity for a sample of Prince's squeal from "Alphabet St.", according to Wikipedia. The song was a US radio hit and an Australian success after the band toured there.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers
years.h: Claude Coleman Jr. joins on drums; Andrew Weiss plays bass
years.p: The duo-with-DAT era ends after ten years. Producer Weiss takes bass and [[Claude Coleman Jr.|75f6f50f-87bd-4f4c-905b-831f3488252f]] becomes the drummer.
years.xp: Magnet says the pair turned Ween into a live band that could play three-hour shows.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chocolate and Cheese · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Chocolate and Cheese: the first Ween record cut in a real studio
years.p: Weiss produces a soul, funk and lounge pile-up; "Freedom of '76" gets a Spike Jonze video.
years.xp:
"Roses Are Free" started turning up in [[Phish|e01646f2-2a04-450d-8bf2-0d993082e058]] setlists in 1997, and Ween started playing it more in response. Gene's verdict on jam bands, printed in Wikipedia: "all that jam band shit makes me want to puke."

About a month earlier they appeared in the Saturday Night Live film It's Pat, which was pulled from theaters a week after opening. In January 1995 they played "I Can't Put My Finger On It" on Late Night with Conan O'Brien.

years.src: The Varsity: A conversation with Dean Ween from 1996 · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: 12 Golden Country Greats: ten songs, Nashville, the Jordanaires
years.p: Recorded in November 1995 with Nashville session players under [[Ben Vaughn|d7a2fd5e-783a-4d5c-893d-4d3fbf249812]]. The title says twelve; the record has ten.
years.xp: Elektra had no idea a country album was coming, Dean told The Varsity: they just "handed it in". The Jordanaires sing on "I'm Holding You" and "Powder Blue".

eras.title: A record about the sea, and the last Elektra album
eras.text: A five-piece lineup that lasts fifteen years, a South Park song, a SpongeBob episode, and a goodbye to the major label.

years.h: Dave Dreiwitz and Glenn McClelland join on bass and keys
years.p: They debut with "The Golden Eel" on Comedy Central's Viva Variety. This lineup holds until 2012.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Mollusk · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers
years.h: The Mollusk: sea shanties, Brit-pop and prog
years.p: Cut in 1996 and 1997 at studios including The Flood Zone in Holgate, New Jersey. Dean calls it "my favorite record we've ever done".
years.xp: Reviews split: Pitchfork gave it a 9.7, Entertainment Weekly a C, NME a 2 out of 10. Dean told Magnet an A&R executive left the finished album on his desk for two weeks unheard. Kurt Vile later named "Mutilated Lips" his favorite song ever.

years.src: Wikipedia: White Pepper · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: White Pepper: Ween's last Elektra record is a pop album
years.p: [[Trey Parker|b8e4771f-6156-48cd-ab77-d10bc3fd50d9]] and [[Matt Stone|8b4844b3-70d6-4507-bc3f-85d09a8e35cd]] of South Park direct the "Even If You Don't" video. The album sells 72,000 copies in the US by November 2002, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Ween had already given Parker and Stone "Love" for Orgazmo in 1997 and "The Rainbow" for the South Park episode "Chef Aid" in 1998. Dean says they're "good friends"; Gene calls them "kindred spirits".

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: The Mollusk · Wikipedia: Ocean Man
years.h: SpongeBob's creator wants a Ween song
years.p: Stephen Hillenburg cites The Mollusk as an inspiration and asks for music; "Loop de Loop" plays in the episode "Your Shoe's Untied".
years.xp: "Ocean Man" closes The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie in 2004. In late 2015 and early 2016 an internet meme put the song over other movies' end credits, and Wikipedia says it became Ween's most-listened track on Spotify and Apple Music.

eras.title: Chocodog, a car crash, a divorce, rehab
eras.text: After Elektra, Ween starts its own label, hits a run of bad luck, and makes its darkest record.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Ween play GodWeenSatan front to back, as a duo, with the DAT
years.p: At John and Peter's in New Hope, to mark the reissue, Gene and Dean re-create the original two-man lineup. Taping is banned.
years.xp: The show came out in 2016 as GodWeenSatan Live. That same year, 2001, Ween formed Chocodog Records, whose first release was the website-only Live in Toronto CD from their October 1996 tour with the Shit Creek Boys.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Quebec (album)
years.h: Claude Coleman is badly hurt in a car accident on Route 78
years.p: Coleman breaks his back and pelvis near Newark. Ween play benefit shows at Bowery Ballroom in New York, October 7 and 8.
years.xp: [[Josh Freese|1ba97964-8d70-4b33-a361-d1a4ed222672]] of the Vandals filled in on those shows and on the next album. Coleman was back for an acoustic set in Brooklyn in December, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Quebec (album)
years.h: Quebec: Sanctuary, Josh Freese and Gene's divorce
years.p: Ween's first album in three years is their darkest. Gene says most of the songs were written just before his marriage ended.
years.xp:
Dean's own take, quoted in Wikipedia: "I don't listen to any of our records, but I have never listened to that one." The Wikipedia page for the album also notes Dean was struggling with substance abuse during the sessions. Dean tells a story of cutting a guitar solo on Carlos Santana's gear in a shipping facility in ten minutes "without getting caught".

In November 2003 came All Request Live, a studio set chosen by fan vote that includes all five parts of "The Stallion".

years.h: Live in Chicago: the Vic Theatre, November 2003
years.p: A CD and DVD of the Quebec tour, shot at Chicago's Vic Theatre.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: A Midwest tour is canceled so Gene can enter alcohol rehab
years.p: After a San Diego show, manager Greg Frey cites "a problem within the band". Ween take a year off the road.
years.xp: Frey's statement said the problem "requires immediate intervention, for the health, welfare, and safety of one of its members". Ween came back in October 2005.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Magnet: Ween, A Band Of Superbad Brothers
years.h: La Cucaracha: the last studio album, on Rounder
years.p: Gene will later call it "a big piece of shit" and place the sessions at the point when he and Dean were "finito".
years.xp: In Magnet, a month or so earlier, he'd said the record was "going to dwarf everything we've ever done". The band had written over 50 songs at a farmhouse studio in 2006 first. The Friends EP preceded the album.

eras.title: Two careers, one bad night in Vancouver
eras.text: Gene goes solo and Dean gets a boat. Then a January 2011 show in Vancouver goes wrong on stage, and by May 2012 Freeman has told Rolling Stone he's retiring Gene Ween.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Dean Ween
years.h: Gene starts solo acoustic shows; Dean earns a captain's license
years.p: Freeman plays as "Gene Ween" alone, then with a band that includes Dave Dreiwitz and drummer Joe Russo. Dean becomes a licensed fishing boat captain.
years.xp: Dean ran a web series called the Brownie Troop Fishing Show and offered trips through Mickey's Guide Service at the Jersey Shore. His captain's license came in 2009 per Wikipedia.

years.big: Dean and Dave walked off mid-song.
years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Gene Ween
years.h: Vancouver: the show that came apart
years.p: At the Queen Elizabeth Theatre, Gene sings off-key, lies on the stage during "Superstar", and finishes the last four songs alone.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia's account, Freeman played tambourine off the beat, sang off-key throughout, and was visibly intoxicated. During "Birthday Boy" Dean and bassist Dreiwitz walked off while Coleman and McClelland swapped instruments. The Seattle show the next night went fine.

Freeman later wrote a song about it, "Covert Discretion": "You don't blow it on stage, lying on your back, screaming nonsense in front of 5,000 people and not try to change something."

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Westword: Gene Ween on Ween's history
years.h: Three nights at Denver's Fillmore, and nobody knows it's the end
years.p: It's Ween's last show for more than four years. The final song is "The Blarney Stone".
years.xp: Gene wrote "The Blarney Stone" after a day with tattoo artist Joel Rose, a proud Scotsman who showed up with a Scottish sword; they dueled, then Gene went home and wrote it, he told Westword.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Gene Ween
years.h: Freeman tells Rolling Stone he's retiring Gene Ween
years.p: That is Dean's reply to the press, and the band's manager had announced the split in June. On July 20 he adds that as long as he and Freeman are alive, Ween is still together, and the idea of quitting is "just laughable".
years.xp: In June, manager Greg Frey told fans on Facebook that Freeman wanted to "more fully explore and pursue his solo career". Freeman's solo album Marvelous Clouds, covers of Rod McKuen songs, had come out about three weeks earlier. Freeman later said he'd left after years of drug and alcohol abuse that got worse on the 2011 tour.

eras.title: Back from the dead, then quiet again
eras.text: Freeman tries a band under his own name, then takes Gene Ween back. The reunion sells out three nights in Colorado and rolls on until Dean steps away from the stage.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween · Wikipedia: Gene Ween
years.h: Ween announce a reunion, two nights at 1stBank Center
years.p: The Broomfield, Colorado shows are set for February 12 and 13, 2016. A third night, February 14, is added because of ticket demand.
years.xp: In between, Freeman had formed a five-piece called Freeman, releasing Free-Man in May 2014, and Dean had started the Dean Ween Group. Freeman on taking the name back: "At the end of the day, people know Gene Ween."

years.src: Westword: Grown, Sober, Still Wild · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Broomfield: three nights, no repeated songs
years.p: Gene opens with "We're Ween. This is Dean Ween; I'm Gene Ween." The first night runs nearly three hours, over thirty songs.
years.xp: Westword noted Dean was sober. Confetti fell during "Roses Are Free" and Gene said: "We wanted it to be dollar bills." The first night was posted free on Archive.org.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Warner releases Bananas and Blow without asking the band
years.p: Dean says the song selection on the compilation feels "random".
years.xp: The band found out about it after the fact, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Ween play Red Rocks for South Park's 25th anniversary
years.p: Primus, Trey Parker and Matt Stone share the bill. Comedy Central airs it August 13.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chocolate and Cheese · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Chocolate and Cheese gets a 30th-anniversary reissue
years.p: Remastered by Bernie Grundman, with 15 outtakes and demos. It sells more than 5,000 vinyl copies in its first week and hits number 15 on Billboard's Top Album Sales.
years.xp: The reissue headlined a 40th-anniversary year that was meant to end with the whole album played at Philadelphia's Mann Center.

years.src: BrooklynVegan: Ween stepping away · Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Ween step away from the stage "for the foreseeable future"
years.p: The band says touring "is too taxing on Deaner's mental health". The Mann Center Philadelphia show is canceled.
years.xp: Dean had said in March, when Southeastern dates were canceled, that he needed to "step away from performing live in order to preserve my mental and spiritual well being". Gene said in August he was "perfectly fine and just as disappointed" about the cancellations.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ween
years.h: Europe '90: a Basel show Dean calls Ween's best ever
years.p: Rhino's Record Store Day release pairs a December 25, 1990 studio session, with an early "Push th' Little Daisies", and a live set from Basel, Switzerland.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Dean described the Basel show as "the best Ween show of all time". A live album of 1996 Foo Fighters opening dates and reissues of White Pepper and Quebec were announced a week later.
